bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **EPR dependency:** ~INR25-30 cr/yr at PBT level (stable) — ex-EPR, underlying PBT growth is muted (analyst math: FY26 PBT INR72 cr − INR21 cr EPR ≈ INR51 cr; Q1 PBT INR28 cr − ~INR5 cr EPR ≈ INR23 cr). EPR accounting (recognised on portal reflection, monetised later) distorts QoQ comparability.
- **West-Asia geopolitics:** double-edged — helps infra (rubberized-bitumen substitution) but hurts consumer/turfing (imported binder prices tripled) and Oman/Saudi logistics; management concedes a severe global escalation would hit everyone.
- **New-geography startup losses** (S.Africa/Saudi) and **new-product ramp** (TPO/rCB) are front-ended costs before revenue.
- **Q2 seasonality** (monsoon) on infrastructure; delayed monsoon a mild positive this year.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material (End-of-Life Tyre feedstock) availability, quality and price volatility — Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table with negative financial implications. Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions can significantly impact cost structures, production timelines and overall operational efficiency; for a business dependent on consistent input of end-of-life materials, regulatory changes, geopolitical tensions, market competition and variability in collection and segregation of scrap add complexity, and inconsistent quality or availability of feedstock can affect product performance and customer satisfaction. Mitigation is supplier diversification across geographies, long-term supplier partnerships, continuous monitoring of raw material markets, investment in material recovery innovations and process flexibility, buffer inventories and local sourcing.
- Emerging and evolving regulation, including dependence on external regulatory bodies — Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material issues table. Dependencies on external stakeholders such as regulatory bodies and customers, together with imbalances in demand and supply dynamics, create uncertainty; developmental issues with regulations including data inconsistencies and technical bottlenecks contribute to residual risk and potential disruptions. The Company has dedicated resources tracking policy developments, is investing in digital systems for accurate data management and real-time reporting on its obligations, and participates in industry forums and consultative processes.
- High capital intensity and investment requirements of tyre recycling — The MD&A Risks and Concerns section names high investment requirements as a major industry risk, and the Opportunities and Threats section names high operating costs as a leading strategic threat. This constrains returns if new capacity does not ramp as planned.
- Uncertain end-markets for recycled products and competition from cheaper disposal alternatives — MD&A lists uncertain markets for recycled products and fluctuating recycled product markets among the biggest strategic threats and major risks. Realisation on recycled output depends on adoption by tyre makers and infrastructure users; the Company states that diversified recycled product markets and strong collection networks are how such risk is managed. MD&A separately names competition from cheaper disposal alternatives as a strategic threat and competition from alternative waste management methods as a major industry risk - a structural constraint on both feedstock economics and pricing power.
- Technology limitations and execution risk in advanced recycling processes — MD&A cites technology challenges and technology limitations among the major risks and threats, and states that companies investing in efficient technology are better positioned. Since the growth thesis rests on higher-value recovery routes such as recovered carbon black and pyrolysis, technology shortfalls would directly impair the product-mix upgrade.
- Geopolitical disruption raising energy, transport and supply-chain costs, and delaying overseas projects — MD&A states the West Asia war is likely to create short-term cost pressure for tyre recyclers because of higher energy and transport costs, though it may strengthen the industry over the medium to long term by making recycled materials more attractive versus petroleum-based virgin materials. The Chairman cum Managing Director's message ties the start of construction of the proposed 24,000 MTPA Saudi Arabia tyre recycling facility, expected during mid-FY27, to normalisation of geopolitical conditions in the Middle East, and the Joint Managing Director notes geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and fluctuating commodity prices in the operating environment.
- Execution and ramp-up risk across the international expansion programme — Phase I of the South Africa project has been completed with operations commenced and exports of semi-processed material underway, but the facility is only expected to achieve operational breakeven in coming quarters; Phase II, enabling full-scale tyre recycling, targets commercial crumb rubber production during Q2 FY27, and the Saudi facility is still at the land-allocation stage. Delivery of the Vision 2029 goal of expanding from 8 to 10 manufacturing locations and nearly doubling revenue to Rs. 1,000 crore depends on these ramps.
- Safety and environmental exposure inherent to recycling operations — MD&A lists safety and environmental concerns among the major risks in the tyre recycling industry, alongside regulatory pressures. The Board's Report describes a risk management framework that identifies and evaluates business risks, is embedded in critical business activities and processes, and reviews changes in the nature and extent of major risks with control measures and future action plans.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26 Tinna expanded its tyre crushing capacity in India by 9% to 185,000 TPA (from 170,000 TPA in FY25) and is targeting capacity of 235,000 TPA in India by FY27, a further 27% increase from current levels. The Company invested approximately Rs 107 crore in capital expenditure during FY26 and has earmarked an additional Rs 100 crore of capex over FY27-FY28 towards enhancing manufacturing capabilities, expanding product offerings and strengthening operational infrastructure. QIP proceeds of approximately Rs 78.7 crore (raised with participation from ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Bank of India Mutual Fund) were fully deployed, including towards capital expenditure for expansion and upgradation of the manufacturing facilities at Varle and Gummidipoondi, repayment of certain borrowings and general corporate purposes. In the polymer business, the Company commissioned a PP recycled compounding facility in FY26 supplying around 200 MT per month, and expanded PCMB capacity to 18,000 MTPA through a new facility near Panipat commissioned in Q1 FY27 — described in the Chairman's message as the expansion of the polymer compounding facility in Haryana to 18,000 TPA by the end of Q1 FY27. Recovered carbon black (rCB) and tyre pyrolysis oil (TPO) facilities were commissioned, strengthening the integrated recycling ecosystem. The Varale facility achieved over 80% capacity utilisation. On the sustainability side, installed solar capacity was more than tripled from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW alongside increased third-party renewable procurement, with nearly 50% of power requirements expected to be met from renewable sources from FY27 onwards. Rs 5 crore has been allocated to R&D for FY27, and approximately Rs 5.6 crore of non-core assets were monetised during the year against an identified non-core asset base of around Rs 28 crore.

- Consumer segment growth supported by increasing adoption of rubber-based recreational surfaces and an expanding global rubber turf market projected to reach about USD 13.7 billion by 2033 at an 8-9% CAGR, with India among the fastest-growing markets
- Steel segment revenue growth lagged volume growth because of downward volatility in steel prices; the Zibo TAA distributorship is expected to support strong growth momentum in FY27
- Infrastructure segment moderated (revenue down about 7%) on a conscious shift away from commoditised, thin-margin products, and faced an early monsoon, geopolitical uncertainty and limited bitumen availability
- PCMB business operating at about 40% capacity utilisation, providing substantial headroom; masterbatch sales rose to nearly 100 MT per month and the PP recycled compounding facility supplies around 200 MT per month
- TPO and rCB facilities are expected to stabilise and ramp during FY27 and become meaningful contributors to revenue and profitability
- Oman performance was impacted by higher raw material costs and temporary export disruptions from geopolitical tensions in West Asia; corrective sourcing and operational measures are expected to normalise cost structures in coming quarters; the GCC region contributed nearly 60% of total sales

risks.note: Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table with negative financial implications. Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions can significantly impact cost structures, production timelines and overall operational efficiency; for a business dependent on consistent input of end-of-life materials, regulatory changes, geopolitical tensions, market competition and variability in collection and segregation of scrap add complexity, and inconsistent quality or availability of feedstock can affect product performance and customer satisfaction. Mitigation is supplier diversification across geographies, long-term supplier partnerships, continuous monitoring of raw material markets, investment in material recovery innovations and process flexibility, buffer inventories and local sourcing.

MD&A separately names competition from cheaper disposal alternatives as a strategic threat and competition from alternative waste management methods as a major industry risk - a structural constraint on both feedstock economics and pricing power.
risks.risk: Uncertain end-markets for recycled products and competition from cheaper disposal alternatives

risks.risk: Raw material (End-of-Life Tyre feedstock) availability, quality and price volatility
risks.note: Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table with negative financial implications. Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions can significantly impact cost structures, production timelines and overall operational efficiency; for a business dependent on consistent input of end-of-life materials, regulatory changes, geopolitical tensions, market competition and variability in collection and segregation of scrap add complexity, and inconsistent quality or availability of feedstock can affect product performance and customer satisfaction. Mitigation is supplier diversification across geographies, long-term supplier partnerships, continuous monitoring of raw material markets, investment in material recovery innovations and process flexibility, buffer inventories and local sourcing.

risks.risk: Emerging and evolving regulation, including dependence on external regulatory bodies
risks.note: Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material issues table. Dependencies on external stakeholders such as regulatory bodies and customers, together with imbalances in demand and supply dynamics, create uncertainty; developmental issues with regulations including data inconsistencies and technical bottlenecks contribute to residual risk and potential disruptions. The Company has dedicated resources tracking policy developments, is investing in digital systems for accurate data management and real-time reporting on its obligations, and participates in industry forums and consultative processes.

risks.risk: High capital intensity and investment requirements of tyre recycling
risks.note: The MD&A Risks and Concerns section names high investment requirements as a major industry risk, and the Opportunities and Threats section names high operating costs as a leading strategic threat. This constrains returns if new capacity does not ramp as planned.

risks.risk: Uncertain end-markets for recycled products and competition from cheaper disposal alternatives
risks.note: MD&A lists uncertain markets for recycled products and fluctuating recycled product markets among the biggest strategic threats and major risks. Realisation on recycled output depends on adoption by tyre makers and infrastructure users; the Company states that diversified recycled product markets and strong collection networks are how such risk is managed. MD&A separately names competition from cheaper disposal alternatives as a strategic threat and competition from alternative waste management methods as a major industry risk - a structural constraint on both feedstock economics and pricing power.

risks.risk: Technology limitations and execution risk in advanced recycling processes
risks.note: MD&A cites technology challenges and technology limitations among the major risks and threats, and states that companies investing in efficient technology are better positioned. Since the growth thesis rests on higher-value recovery routes such as recovered carbon black and pyrolysis, technology shortfalls would directly impair the product-mix upgrade.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption raising energy, transport and supply-chain costs, and delaying overseas projects
risks.note: MD&A states the West Asia war is likely to create short-term cost pressure for tyre recyclers because of higher energy and transport costs, though it may strengthen the industry over the medium to long term by making recycled materials more attractive versus petroleum-based virgin materials. The Chairman cum Managing Director's message ties the start of construction of the proposed 24,000 MTPA Saudi Arabia tyre recycling facility, expected during mid-FY27, to normalisation of geopolitical conditions in the Middle East, and the Joint Managing Director notes geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and fluctuating commodity prices in the operating environment.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk across the international expansion programme
risks.note: Phase I of the South Africa project has been completed with operations commenced and exports of semi-processed material underway, but the facility is only expected to achieve operational breakeven in coming quarters; Phase II, enabling full-scale tyre recycling, targets commercial crumb rubber production during Q2 FY27, and the Saudi facility is still at the land-allocation stage. Delivery of the Vision 2029 goal of expanding from 8 to 10 manufacturing locations and nearly doubling revenue to Rs. 1,000 crore depends on these ramps.

risks.risk: Safety and environmental exposure inherent to recycling operations
risks.note: MD&A lists safety and environmental concerns among the major risks in the tyre recycling industry, alongside regulatory pressures. The Board's Report describes a risk management framework that identifies and evaluates business risks, is embedded in critical business activities and processes, and reviews changes in the nature and extent of major risks with control measures and future action plans.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Established in 1987, Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Limited is a leading Indian end-of-life tyre (ELT) recycler that converts waste tyres into crumb rubber, micronized rubber powder and reclaimed steel, operating eight manufacturing facilities across India and overseas.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: TRIL processes end-of-life tyres into high-value recycled products such as Crumb Rubber Powder (CRP), Micronized Rubber Powder (MRP) and high tensile Reclaim Rubber, and also offers infrastructure development services. Its integrated circular-economy model spans the value chain from procurement and processing of ELTs to manufacturing specialised recycled rubber products for the infrastructure, industrial, consumer, steel and polymer industries. The Company describes itself as the only company in India manufacturing rubber-based products for both road bitumen and non-road industries, serving customers in India and across export markets.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue FY27: INR675-700 cr** (reiterated); Vision-2029 target **INR1,000 cr by FY29** at **25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profit CAGR, >18% EBITDA margin, >30% ROCE, 10 locations**.
- **Margin:** guided **18-20%** (aspiration 18%+) despite 22% delivered — cautious on front-ended new-business costs; management calls 18-20% "sustainable/systemic."
- **Capacity:** tire-crushing **185,000 → 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27**; MRP expansion **+3,500 tpa commissioning Q3FY27 → 20,000 tpa** (claimed world's largest); blended utilization **75-80% by fiscal-end**.
- **New products:** **TPO (Varle)** — trial Q1, **commercial sales Q2**, stabilise Q3; **rCB** — production Q3, **commercial sales Q4**; TPO+rCB together **7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 cr)**.
- **Segments:** **TP Buildtech >30% growth, cross INR100 cr revenue FY27**; **PCMB → 10% of FY27 revenue**; **Steel Abrasives ~50% volume growth FY27** (Zibo TAA China distributorship, customer transition Q4FY27).
- **International:** Mbodla (S.Africa) **breakeven Q2FY27**, Phase-2 tire-recycling production Q2/Q3; Saudi 24,000 tpa **construction start end-CY2026** (geopolitics permitting).
- **Capex ~INR100 cr FY27-28** (INR60 cr FY27); **R&D INR5 cr FY27**.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **TPO + rCB (pyrolysis)** — the new high-value leg, commercial from Q2/Q3, ~INR50-60 cr in FY27.
- **PCMB** scaling to 18,000 tpa; **Steel Abrasives** via Zibo; **TP Buildtech** to >INR100 cr.
- **International sourcing/hedge:** Chile (new) + South Africa secure end-of-life-tire feedstock; Oman/Saudi are Middle-East processing bases. Possible **new greenfield India plant / de-bottlenecking** as domestic demand is "very robust" at 80-85% utilization.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Waste Tyre Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework is formalising the recycling ecosystem and creating financial incentives for authorised recyclers through tradable EPR certificates; the Company's EPR credit revenue contributed approximately Rs 29 crore during FY26, consistent with the previous year
- Industry transition away from low-value applications such as tyre-derived fuel towards premium recovered products (rCB, reclaimed rubber, pyrolysis oil, recovered steel, speciality chemicals)
- Industrial segment demand driven by rising raw material costs and the sustainability/ESG commitments of tyre manufacturers, with export volumes up about 30% and a healthy order pipeline
- Consumer segment growth supported by increasing adoption of rubber-based recreational surfaces and an expanding global rubber turf market projected to reach about USD 13.7 billion by 2033 at an 8-9% CAGR, with India among the fastest-growing markets
- Steel segment revenue growth lagged volume growth because of downward volatility in steel prices; the Zibo TAA distributorship is expected to support strong growth momentum in FY27
- Infrastructure segment moderated (revenue down about 7%) on a conscious shift away from commoditised, thin-margin products, and faced an early monsoon, geopolitical uncertainty and limited bitumen availability
- PCMB business operating at about 40% capacity utilisation, providing substantial headroom; masterbatch sales rose to nearly 100 MT per month and the PP recycled compounding facility supplies around 200 MT per month
- TPO and rCB facilities are expected to stabilise and ramp during FY27 and become meaningful contributors to revenue and profitability
- Oman performance was impacted by higher raw material costs and temporary export disruptions from geopolitical tensions in West Asia; corrective sourcing and operational measures are expected to normalise cost structures in coming quarters; the GCC region contributed nearly 60% of total sales
- India's tyre recycling industry has the potential to process nearly 4 million tonnes of ELTs annually through formal recycling channels by FY2030; as of March 2026 registered recyclers had processed approximately 12.23 lakh tonnes of waste tyres with around 11.69 lakh tonnes of EPR certificates generated
- Indian polymer composites market projected to grow from about USD 151.5 million in 2024 to USD 208.3 million by 2030 (about 5.5% CAGR) and the Indian masterbatch market from about USD 364.7 million to USD 460.1 million by 2030 (about 4.15% CAGR)
- Global recovered carbon black market projected to reach approximately USD 706 million by 2030 at around 16.4% CAGR, and the Indian tyre recycling market to approximately USD 743.8 million by 2030, with carbon black among the fastest-growing product segments
- Associate TP Buildtech Private Limited commissioned its Kolkata manufacturing facility and introduced three new construction chemical product lines; utilisation is around 15% and is expected to scale progressively during FY27
- India's tyre and automotive industry growth (world's seventh-largest tyre producer, domestic tyre industry revenue expected to more than double by FY2032) will increase ELT availability and feedstock supply
- Industrial segment delivered about 30% YoY growth in export volumes despite global economic headwinds, supported by a healthy order pipeline
- Exports supported by an expanding global customer base and a strong order pipeline, positioning exports as an important pillar of future growth

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross-margin expansion (the bulk of the ~4% EBITDA-margin jump) from (i) more efficient/optional raw-material sourcing and (ii) higher value-added product mix — management calls these **systemic, not one-off** (marginal inventory gain only). Material+inventory-to-sales fell to ~46% (from >51%). Offset: front-ended costs of new geographies (Saudi/S.Africa) and new plants → why 18-20% is guided vs 22% delivered.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Core investment stays **India** ("for the foreseeable future"); international nodes are hedges/sourcing, not the primary capital sink. INR5 cr to R&D (recycled-rubber + engineered plastics + recovered-fiber TPO). RE build-out (rooftop solar Gummidipoondi 999 kW / Varle 2,218 kW; RE 51% of power) to cut energy cost. WC disciplined at ~50 days.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26 Tinna expanded its tyre crushing capacity in India by 9% to 185,000 TPA (from 170,000 TPA in FY25) and is targeting capacity of 235,000 TPA in India by FY27, a further 27% increase from current levels. The Company invested approximately Rs 107 crore in capital expenditure during FY26 and has earmarked an additional Rs 100 crore of capex over FY27-FY28 towards enhancing manufacturing capabilities, expanding product offerings and strengthening operational infrastructure. QIP proceeds of approximately Rs 78.7 crore (raised with participation from ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Bank of India Mutual Fund) were fully deployed, including towards capital expenditure for expansion and upgradation of the manufacturing facilities at Varle and Gummidipoondi, repayment of certain borrowings and general corporate purposes. In the polymer business, the Company commissioned a PP recycled compounding facility in FY26 supplying around 200 MT per month, and expanded PCMB capacity to 18,000 MTPA through a new facility near Panipat commissioned in Q1 FY27 — described in the Chairman's message as the expansion of the polymer compounding facility in Haryana to 18,000 TPA by the end of Q1 FY27. Recovered carbon black (rCB) and tyre pyrolysis oil (TPO) facilities were commissioned, strengthening the integrated recycling ecosystem. The Varale facility achieved over 80% capacity utilisation. On the sustainability side, installed solar capacity was more than tripled from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW alongside increased third-party renewable procurement, with nearly 50% of power requirements expected to be met from renewable sources from FY27 onwards. Rs 5 crore has been allocated to R&D for FY27, and approximately Rs 5.6 crore of non-core assets were monetised during the year against an identified non-core asset base of around Rs 28 crore.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident but deliberately conservative (JMD Gaurav Sekhri repeatedly reframes 22% down to an 18-20% "guidance," citing front-ended costs). Transparent — if repetitive — on the EPR accounting nuance under persistent analyst probing; candid that ex-EPR growth is optical-heavy. COO Subodh detailed on segments; CFO Abhay crisp on capex phasing (INR60 cr FY27). Credible execution track record on MRP scale-up.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated circular economy platform: unlike conventional recyclers that primarily produce crumb rubber, Tinna maximises resource recovery through value-added downstream products
- One of the widest product portfolios in the tyre recycling industry, serving roads, tyres, industrial rubber products, sports infrastructure, steel abrasives and polymer composites, reducing dependence on any single industry
- Stated to be the only company in India manufacturing rubber-based products for both road bitumen and non-road industries
- Strong manufacturing footprint of eight facilities across India and international markets, giving proximity to customers and diversified sourcing
- Technology-led operations, with continuous investment in advanced recycling, process optimisation and product development; commissioning of recovered carbon black (rCB) and tyre pyrolysis oil (TPO) facilities strengthens the integrated recycling ecosystem
- Growing global presence and export franchise with marquee customers in tyre manufacturing, infrastructure, industrial, consumer and steel segments
- Legacy spanning over 35 years with end-to-end integrated manufacturing capability

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **EPR dependency:** ~INR25-30 cr/yr at PBT level (stable) — ex-EPR, underlying PBT growth is muted (analyst math: FY26 PBT INR72 cr − INR21 cr EPR ≈ INR51 cr; Q1 PBT INR28 cr − ~INR5 cr EPR ≈ INR23 cr). EPR accounting (recognised on portal reflection, monetised later) distorts QoQ comparability.
- **West-Asia geopolitics:** double-edged — helps infra (rubberized-bitumen substitution) but hurts consumer/turfing (imported binder prices tripled) and Oman/Saudi logistics; management concedes a severe global escalation would hit everyone.
- **New-geography startup losses** (S.Africa/Saudi) and **new-product ramp** (TPO/rCB) are front-ended costs before revenue.
- **Q2 seasonality** (monsoon) on infrastructure; delayed monsoon a mild positive this year.
- Guidance-vs-delivery gap (18-20% guide vs 22% print) — manage expectations.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The clean read is EPR-adjusted:** EPR (~INR25-30 cr/yr PBT, stable) is now "integral" but flat — so the growth engine is genuinely the volume/mix shift (MRP +28%, Reclaim +37%, exports +46%, Industrial rev +58%), not EPR.
- **This quarter's EPR cash (~INR25 cr) is a balance-sheet event** (inventory→cash), not a P&L event — analysts repeatedly conflated the two; management held the line.
- **Vision re-labelled 2028 → 2029** (INR1,000 cr now by FY29) and near-term crushing target sharpened to **235k tpa by FY27** (vs "250k by FY28" last covered quarter) — a modest timeline/scope reset.
- **New Chile subsidiary** signals feedstock security is becoming a strategic priority (hedging global ELP supply), alongside S.Africa.
- Rubberized bitumen is structurally advantaged by permanent Indian bitumen-import dependence + government import-reduction push — a durable infra tailwind independent of the current price spike.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Vision 2029: transform into a globally recognised integrated circular materials company, expanding presence from 8 to 10 locations and nearly doubling revenue to Rs 1,000 crore by FY2029, supported by disciplined capital allocation and continuous investment in advanced recycling technologies
- Shift the product mix towards specialised, higher-value products such as Modified Rubber Powder, Crumb Rubber Modifier and Reclaimed Rubber that offer better margins, stronger customer stickiness and higher entry barriers
- In the Infrastructure business, consciously choose profitability over low-margin …
